headline: US Crude Oil Inventories Increase by 3.4 Million Barrels
summary: U.S. commercial crude oil inventories rose by 3.4 million barrels for the week ending November 13, reaching 417.8 million barrels. This level remains 3% below the five-year average for this period.
why: Oil inventory data from the EIA is a key indicator of supply-demand balance in the energy market, often influencing global crude oil prices.

impacts.name: WTI Crude Oil
impacts.why: Rising inventories typically signal an oversupply, which can exert downward pressure on oil prices.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: An unexpected or significant increase in crude stockpiles suggests lower demand or higher supply, which generally leads to lower oil prices.
